title: Judges 13
paragraphs: ¹ Again the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD handed them over to the Philistines for forty years. ² A certain man of Zorah, from the tribe of Dan, whose name was Manoah, had a wife who was barren and had borne no children. ³ The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "You are barren and childless, but you are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son. ⁴ Now then, be careful not to drink wine or other fermented drink and not to eat anything unclean. ⁵ You will become pregnant and have a son whose head is never to be touched by a razor, because the boy will be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from the womb. He will begin the deliverance of Israel from the Philistines."

⁶ Then the woman went and told her husband: "A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God — very awe-inspiring. I didn't ask him where he came from, and he didn't tell me his name. ⁷ But he said to me, 'You are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son. Don't drink wine or other fermented drink and don't eat anything unclean, because the boy will be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from birth until the day of his death.'" ⁸ Then Manoah prayed to the LORD: "Please, Lord, let the man of God you sent come to us again to teach us how to raise the boy who is to be born." ⁹ God heard Manoah's prayer, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field. But her husband Manoah was not with her. ¹⁰ The woman hurried to tell her husband, "The man who appeared to me the other day is here!"

¹¹ Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he asked, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?" "I am," he said. ¹² Manoah asked, "When your word comes true, what will be the rules for the boy's life and work?" ¹³ The angel of the LORD replied, "Let the woman pay attention to everything I told her. ¹⁴ She must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, nor drink wine or other fermented drink, nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I commanded her." ¹⁵ Then Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Please stay and let us prepare a young goat for you."

¹⁶ The angel of the LORD replied, "Even if you keep me here, I will not eat your food. But if you want to prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." For Manoah did not yet realize that it was the angel of the LORD. ¹⁷ Then Manoah asked the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes true?" ¹⁸ The angel of the LORD replied, "Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding." ¹⁹ Then Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering and sacrificed them on a rock to the LORD. And the LORD did something remarkable while Manoah and his wife watched. ²⁰ As the flame blazed up from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame. Seeing this, Manoah and his wife fell face down on the ground.

²¹ The angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah realized it was the angel of the LORD. ²² "We are going to die!" he said to his wife. "We have seen God!" ²³ But his wife replied, "If the LORD had meant to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hands, nor shown us all these things, nor told us this at this time." ²⁴ The woman gave birth to a boy and named him Samson. The child grew and the LORD blessed him. ²⁵ The Spirit of the LORD began to stir him while he was in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
